# Source-only native ALC ownership plan

This implementation has not been compiled or executed. Proof CLI mode remains unavailable. The existing help and malformed-argument controls continue without a wrapper. No compiler, Boogie, solver flag, query, seed, hash implementation, or resource reply is changed.

The API keeps the existing `MainWithWriters` verification path. Construct a single-use `NativeProofSupervisor` with the real solver path/digest, an explicitly delegated cgroup-v2 parent, an existing evidence parent, and Python. A private generated wrapper is pinned to the static source-manifest template digest. The caller must use that exact wrapper in its one explicit `--solver-path`; no environment fallback exists. The first native control set is the true, false, and fuel source fixtures; these are future execution inputs, not proof evidence.

The current supervisor is Linux x64 only. The delegated cgroup must be a private, empty domain group under `/sys/fs/cgroup`, contain no live processes or child groups, and permit the caller to create/delete its own leaf and write `cgroup.kill`. The supervisor never alters the parent configuration. Missing delegation, pidfds or required permissions fails before loading a product. It pins the parent and its own child directory handles, revalidates their exact kernel paths/private parent before draining, and opens `cgroup.kill` relative to that pinned child handle. A random exclusive leaf is the ownership boundary: launched wrappers join it before forking, and descendants inherit membership even when reparented or creating new process sessions. This is stronger than a process-tree snapshot. The API assumes the delegated parent is supplied by a trusted CI setup and cannot be written by an unrelated actor; same-UID hostile actors are outside this bounded scratch gate. Linux arm64 directory-open flag ABI is not yet reviewed and is rejected.

Launch admission and closure share a Linux flock. Each launch records the wrapper and solver PID, kernel start time, parent, process group/session, sealed solver-image digest/length/seals, and exact solver argument array. The solver child waits on a pipe before exec until the supervisor verifies ancestry, exclusive-cgroup membership and pre/post pidfd identity, captures both pidfds, and atomically publishes the complete acknowledgement token by same-directory rename. Thus even a short version probe is recorded before it can execute/exit. Within the stated caps, every discovered live cgroup member receives a pidfd; no numeric PID or group number alone authorizes a signal. Process groups/sessions are evidence, not a global `killpg` permission. Bounds are 64 launches, 256 live members, 4096 historical identities, 256 MiB per executable image and 64 MiB per captured stream; each identity receives at most one request per signal, so cleanup polling cannot inflate its ledger.

The wrapper uses binary `os.read`/`os.write`, handles partial/interrupted writes, independently drains stderr, records EOF/OS errors, and logs exact byte streams with read/write counts and SHA-256 digests. It does not decode or modify SMT commands or replies. It copies the bounded regular native ELF solver into an executable memfd, requires `F_SEAL_WRITE|F_SEAL_GROW|F_SEAL_SHRINK|F_SEAL_SEAL`, verifies the resulting seals, hashes the final sealed bytes against the configured pin, rewinds and executes that captured descriptor. In-place source mutation during or after capture cannot alter the sealed executed image; a capture with different bytes fails its digest. `MFD_EXEC` requires Linux 6.3 or newer and executable-memfd support; missing support fails without pathname/unsealed fallback. It preserves the original solver path as argv[0], argument values and environment. Descriptor execution changes `/proc/self/exe` and may change `$ORIGIN` dependency lookup: before transparency acceptance, the pinned Z3 package must be shown self-contained with respect to executable-origin resources. This is not an arbitrary-executable transparency guarantee.

The wrapper verifies the host process start time before/after opening its pidfd and watches that process descriptor; retiring the .NET thread that created the wrapper cannot trigger wrapper death. Its watcher begins after the Python fork. Host process exit kills only the wrapper itself. The solver child retains `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` because its creating Python main thread waits for it and remains alive; no wrapper-host creating-thread assumption exists. A dead host cannot produce a cleanup receipt, and CI must independently retain ownership of delegated cgroup teardown. Wrapper-internal diagnostics stay in evidence files and never contaminate solver streams. Logging and handshake overhead affect elapsed time, so wall deadlines remain safety caps; no RU correction is permitted.

After CLI completion (including its results/logs), close launch admission, signal only owned non-wrapper pidfds, and allow wrappers to drain streams/reap solvers/exit. The normal phase uses at most half the caller's safety deadline, monitor shutdown at most one eighth (capped at one second), reserving the remainder for a final drain. Normal ledger-lock acquisition is bounded. Admission-lock, scan/cap, signal, monitor and metadata failures cannot skip the `finally` drain: cancel the monitor, atomically mark admission closed if flock closure failed, then attempt authoritative emptiness/removal or at most eight fd-relative `cgroup.kill` requests within the deadline. Even an already expired deadline permits one drain attempt. Membership/event read failure does not suppress the kill after exact leaf ownership is revalidated. Failure to revalidate ownership prohibits signaling and leaves a fatal failure receipt requiring host shutdown. No numeric PID, foreign cgroup or unrelated process is a fallback authority.

Every fallback/fault poisons the host even if the group is subsequently empty. Forced wrapper termination leaves stream completeness unproven. The final empty member list plus `cgroup.events populated 0` and successful kernel removal close late-join races, including a wrapper that had passed admission before failed flock closure. Disposal also attempts a separate five-second owned drain after unsuccessful/omitted cleanup; it cannot convert failure to success and writes a separate failure-only disposal receipt. A successful cleanup receipt requires nonempty complete launch records, exact read/write stream equality, zero relay failures, zero live captured pidfds and removed empty cgroup. It binds the exact parsed completion bytes and all three captured stream digests/lengths plus validation facts into `cleanup.json`; the returned SHA-256 is computed from those exact serialized cleanup bytes. Missing/changed identity, monitor faults, incomplete receipts or cleanup failures remain explicit. This assumes evidence is not modified by an unrelated same-UID actor after owned writers have exited.

Normal wrapper exit reaches Boogie `SMTLibProcess.SolverExited` and `DisposeProver`, which removes its own Console.CancelKeyPress handler (pinned source `73a0e214`, `Source/Provers/SMTLib/SMTLibProcess.cs`). This implementation neither edits shared event backing fields nor claims to dispose an uncaptured engine. The actual private scheduler must still be disposed, and the existing long weak reference must become dead before another context starts. If solver shutdown does not permit actual ALC collection, the whole-CLI design is blocked; do not silently weaken unload or detach global handlers.

Pending mandatory controls before enabling proof CLI: compile/API review; cgroup delegation failure; absent/wrong solver/template digest; source-inode mutation after capture and seal/write refusal; executable memfd and pinned Z3 origin-resource checks; refused late launch; acknowledgement-publication scheduling race; short probe ownership; partial-write/EOF/stderr/error forwarding; timeout and descendant/reparenting cleanup; more than 256 simultaneously live owned descendants (must fail the cap, still drain to empty/remove, record fallback and poison); admission-lock/monitor/membership-read failure cleanup; creating-parent-thread exit while host stays alive (wrapper/solver must stay alive), followed by host-process exit control; pid reuse rejection; incomplete receipt rejection; real native true/false/fuel outcomes with nonzero proof-batch denominators; actual context unload and framework witness stability; exact source/toolchain/hash receipts. Historical short-lived descendants that vanish between scans are not individually enumerated; authoritative cgroup emptiness establishes the live-process cleanup boundary. Stream equality currently authenticates forwarding, not complete SMT-query/RU denominators. Full native-query/resource comparisons and broader P1 gates remain separate work.
